summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder, was admitted with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and urinalysis findings consistent with a urinary tract infection. Chest imaging showed no acute pulmonary process, and symptoms of respiratory infection improved during the stay. Urine culture grew Escherichia coli, sensitive to ampicillin/sulbactam, and blood cultures remained negative. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral Augmentin at discharge. His baclofen pump refill was deferred, but oral baclofen was provided for muscle spasms. He received education on improved catheterization hygiene and frequency to reduce future infection risk. He was discharged home with services and instructions to follow up with his specialists.
